description: Past Indian flood events for Sentinel-1 flood change. Each entry is a fetch request for `python -m backend.sentinel1 --event <event_id>`: an AOI that fits one Process API request and inclusive UTC date windows. Facts come only from the listed sources; anything not yet checked against data is listed under `unverified`.

events.name: Kosi flood after the record Birpur barrage release

aoi.label: Kiratpur block, Darbhanga district
aoi.derivation: Bounding box of OpenStreetMap relation 10286965 (Kiratpur), from Nominatim on 2026-10-05.

events.window_rationale: The before window ends ahead of the 28 September release; the after window starts the day of the 29 September breach. Only Sentinel-1A was flying, so each window spans at least one 12-day repeat of every track.

sources.supports: 661,000 cusecs released from Birpur barrage till late night on 28 September 2024, the highest since 1968; the Kosi western embankment breached near Bhubhol village, Darbhanga district, late on 29 September.
Kiratpur and Ghanshyampur blocks of Darbhanga were among the worst flooded after the western embankment breach.
Sentinel-1B stopped on 23 December 2021, leaving Sentinel-1A alone.

unverified: Sentinel-1 acquisitions on one shared track exist in both windows.
The before window is free of earlier monsoon flooding in this block.

events.name: Barak river flood through the Bethukandi embankment breach

aoi.label: Silchar town and surroundings, Cachar district
aoi.derivation: 20 km square centred on OpenStreetMap node 567777060 (Silchar, place=city), from Nominatim on 2026-10-06. The square is a declared choice; Nominatim's own box for the node is a fixed-size placeholder, not a boundary.

events.window_rationale: Flooding began on 19 June and the town stayed submerged for 11 days. Only Sentinel-1A was flying, so each window spans at least one 12-day repeat of every track.

sources.supports: Floods from 19 to 30 June 2022 caused by a breach of the Barak river dyke at Bethukandi; Silchar city remained submerged for 11 days.
Sentinel-1B stopped on 23 December 2021, leaving Sentinel-1A alone.

unverified: Sentinel-1 acquisitions on one shared track exist in both windows.
The before window is free of earlier flooding in Cachar.

events.name: August 2018 Kerala flood on the Periyar at Aluva

aoi.label: Aluva and the lower Periyar floodplain, Ernakulam district
aoi.derivation: 20 km square centred on OpenStreetMap node 1880437827 (Aluva, place=town), from Nominatim on 2026-10-06. The square is a declared choice, not a boundary.

events.window_rationale: CWC dates the first onset of flooding to the end of July, so the before window ends on 25 July; the after window covers the 14-19 August spell. Sentinel-1A and 1B were both flying, a 6-day repeat per track.

sources.supports: Central Water Commission, Study Report: Kerala Floods of August 2018 (September 2018): first onset of flooding towards the end of July; a severe spell on 8-9 August; another from 14 to 19 August causing disastrous flooding in 13 of 14 districts; the Periyar sub-basin is analysed in section 4.1.

unverified: Sentinel-1 acquisitions on one shared track exist in both windows.
The Aluva AOI itself was dry in the before window.
